clue.text: Get rid of mess from small — very small — dog

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
wee is Scottish and informal for very small
a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: Someone must clear up what a tiny little dog has left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear away debris or disorder is to tidy it, getting rid of the mess.

clue.text: See 24
Sesame seed appears around end of season in bulk

indicators.note: around puts the jumbled letters about the final letter
to seed is to scatter, so the letters are scattered
end of picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Sesame seeds turn up in large quantities by the season's close.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seed' rearranges SESAME as EMASSE, which goes 'around' the N ending 'season'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means all together as a group, that is in bulk.

clue.text: Huntsman …

parts.note: a fox hunter is named after the colour of the scarlet coat he wears

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue, which uses this answer as a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Fox hunters' scarlet coats are called pinks, and by extension a rider wearing one is so called.

clue.text: … holding up taxi, getting seasoner drunk, to pay close attention

indicators.note: holding means the huntsman's word contains the taxi

parts.note: the ellipsis carries on from the previous clue, whose answer is the huntsman

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the taxi is read bottom to top

parts.note: a cab is a taxi

indicators.note: drunk shows the letters are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: A hunter holds up a cab and gets the seasoner drunk, while listening carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: PINK, the huntsman, comes from the previous clue via the ellipsis; 'up' turns the taxi round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: This idiom means to listen attentively, like an animal pricking its ears.

clue.text: Trench mortar, signalled, came to 1,000 odd

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters of the preceding words are strangely arranged

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A First World War weapon's message seemed to add up to a strange thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges CAMETO plus M. In the old army signalling alphabet T was 'Toc' and M 'Emma', so a TM (trench mortar) was signalled as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: First World War signallers spelt out T and M with phonetic code words, giving the trench mortar its nickname.

clue.text: Writer from the fringe (clue found in the Rubaiyat)

parts.note: read the solution as wordplay: the word the, then fringe's letters on the move giving the anagram of a digit

explanation.surface: An author from the edge of things, said to be quoted in Persian poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: In FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam 'The Moving Finger writes'; the phrase is itself a clue, the anagram indicator 'moving' turning FINGER into 'fringe'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the famous quatrain a finger moves on writing, so it is a writer of fate.

clue.text: Superior housekeeper in conversation with "the lily maid"

parts.note: a chat is a conversation
Elaine is the lily maid of Astolat in Tennyson's Arthurian poems

explanation.surface: A grand housekeeper talks with a famous Arthurian maiden.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistress of a large household or castle, in charge of its keeping.

clue.text: 18 15 — swallow one!

parts.note: a martin is a bird of the swallow family
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cocktail order with an invitation to knock one back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' looks like the drinking verb but is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The original version of this cocktail mixes gin with Italian vermouth.

clue.text: Girl keeps Manx cat as part of healing process

indicators.note: keeps means the girl holds the cat within her

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

indicators.note: a Manx cat has no tail, so the last letter is docked

parts.note: a tiger is a big cat

explanation.surface: A girl's tailless pet helps her recover.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreign substance prompting the body to make antibodies plays a part in fighting infection.

clue.text: Chimney in an establishment that shows brightness

parts.note: lum is a Scottish and northern word for a chimney
taken as written
CE is the Church of England, the established church

explanation.surface: A chimney in some institution apparently gives off light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Establishment' church in England is the Church of England, abbreviated CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Luminance is the technical measure of how bright a surface appears.

clue.text: A scared demon?

parts.note: frit is a dialect word for frightened, from northern England

explanation.surface: Can a demon itself be frightened?
explanation.definitionFit: In Arabic mythology an afrit is a powerful evil spirit or demon.

clue.text: Too necessary part in choral society

indicators.note: a necessary part of these words is a run of their letters sitting inside them

explanation.surface: Another essential role in a choir.
explanation.definitionFit: Too and also are synonyms, both meaning in addition.

clue.text: Killing in bygone territorial army style

indicators.note: style here suggests the letters are fashioned into a new shape

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Death dealt the way the old reservists did it.
explanation.definitionFit: Stabbing someone with the blade fixed to a rifle is a way of killing them.

clue.text: Container for mushroom in claret cooked on earth

indicators.note: on puts the jumbled wine above the next piece in this down entry
in places the mushroom within the jumbled wine
cooked suggests the letters have been doctored

parts.note: a cep is an edible mushroom, the porcini
E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: A dish for mushrooms cooked in red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The mushroom goes into the claret after its letters are 'cooked' into RETACL; botanically a receptacle is also part of a fungus, hence 'for mushroom'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything that holds or receives items is a container; botanists also use the word for a fungus's base.

clue.text: Old maker of music about stream

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a beck is a northern English word for a brook

explanation.surface: An ancient musician performs on the subject of a brook.
explanation.definitionFit: The rebeck is a medieval bowed string instrument, so a maker of music from long ago.

clue.text: See 18
Successive notes among followers in part exchange

indicators.note: among places the notes amid the letters of the followers

parts.note: a train is a retinue of followers
D and E are consecutive notes of the scale

explanation.surface: Music played by an entourage during a swap.
explanation.definitionFit: Handing over an old item as partial payment for a new one is a part exchange.

clue.text: Queen abandons season but returns, going round to do the washing

indicators.note: going round means the reversed word encloses the cut season
returns means the word but is read backwards
abandons means the queen leaves the season's letters

parts.note: winter is a season
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: The queen gives up on winter but comes back to do the laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' cuts ER from WINTER to WINT; 'returns' makes TUB of BUT.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old washing machine with separate washing and spinning drums, used for laundry.

clue.text: Once more the good guy's in opposition

parts.note: again means once more
ST is short for saint, a good person

explanation.surface: Again, the hero finds himself on the other side.
explanation.definitionFit: To be opposed to something is to be against it.

clue.text: Drink has trap with it

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for animals
and means together with
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in the cocktail gin and it

explanation.surface: A drink that comes with a snare attached.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's pronoun 'it' is the abbreviation of the vermouth's nationality, the 'it' of a 'gin and it'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cocktail of gin mixed with sweet Italian vermouth.

clue.text: Writer turning to melody in Holst's work

indicators.note: turning means the word for writer is turned round

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: An author takes up a tune in a composer's piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune, the Mystic, is the last movement of Holst's suite The Planets.

clue.text: Endless Irish tact in work of crude style

indicators.note: work suggests the letters are worked into another form
endless means the last letter of the word is cut off

explanation.surface: A tactless Irish piece of work that lacks refinement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' turns Irish into IRIS; 'work' rearranges IRISTACTIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lacking artistic skill or taste is crude in its style.

clue.text: Throw up s-seat

parts.note: the stammered start of the word repeats its first letter
pew is a church seat

explanation.surface: Someone stammers out a word for a seat before being sick.
explanation.walkthrough: The stutter repeats the first letter of the seat: S then PEW.
explanation.definitionFit: To vomit is to bring food back up, a crude synonym.

clue.text: Tired, ie be clothed, with the unknown?

parts.note: to wear is to be clothed in something
Y is a mathematical unknown, like x

explanation.surface: Dressed and wondering about the unknown, one is exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Weary and tired are synonyms meaning lacking energy.

clue.text: Large request to look at capital

parts.note: OS is outsize, a large clothing size
lo is an old word asking someone to look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: A big request to view the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital city of Norway.

clue.text: Musical approach for sequel to 18 left in seat

parts.note: the drink in 18 across is gin, and tonic is what follows gin in the familiar pairing

indicators.note: in places the left inside the seat

parts.note: a sofa is a seat

explanation.surface: A musical method for following a drink, found in a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a system of teaching singing using syllables such as do, re, mi for the notes.

clue.text: Sequel to 18, making it 3, infuriates stout characters keeping half-hearted rabbit inside

indicators.note: keeping means the anger word holds the rest within it

parts.note: angers means infuriates

indicators.note: inside places the shortened rabbit within the jumbled letters
the characters of stout means its letters, mixed up
half-hearted removes one of the two middle letters, half its heart

explanation.surface: A drink that follows gin angers stout characters with a rabbit in them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' rearranges STOUT to OSTUT, with RABIT (one heart letter gone) inside after OSTU. 3 is PINK: these bitters turn gin into pink gin.
explanation.definitionFit: A dash of these aromatic bitters added to gin makes the drink called pink gin.

clue.text: See 25
Authority for queen in old king's nest site

indicators.note: in places the approval and the queen within the king

parts.note: roy is an archaic spelling of roi, French for king
OK means permission or authority, as in give the OK
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Permission for a queen to stay in an old monarch's nest.
explanation.definitionFit: A colony of rooks' nests in treetops is a classic nesting site.
